headline: Airport director presents plan for consolidated car rental facility, funded by customer fees, with $1.9 million collected so far.
summary: The airport director said a long-term facility could cost $20-30 million and would pay for itself over time through the fees. Money now collected would cover planning and design, with construction funds ready within a few years. Also up for second reading is an order to create a full-time department head to oversee the Community Connector transit system, with up to $65,000 from the unassigned fund balance.
discussion: Transit department head: Members asked about ridership and pay. Staff said ridership has grown steadily but is stagnant, and that reliable service would help bring riders back; pay would start in the low $100,000s, up to around 150.

Airport car rental facility: The airport director said the project is in the airport's master plan and is paid for by fees collected since March, about $1.9 million so far. Asked whether city funds would be needed, the director said the project would be self-sustaining.
Council training: Staff said onboarding for new councilors will be split into two shorter sessions, with legal training first and a second training set for December 16th.

City solicitor: Dave Sauerzapf's last council meeting and last day are being marked, and Assistant City Solicitor Grace Ennis will serve as interim solicitor. Recruiting for the role will be discussed at the next council meeting.
